title: Nsila motorcycle-taxi strike over gendarmerie formalities
location: Nzila/Nsila gendarmerie barrier, about 11 km south of Bangui
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The source says motorcycle conductors serving the Nsila road went on strike and barricaded the road, but gives no count of people present together. Occupation membership, vehicles, and affected traffic are not participant counts.

title.summary: Both reports describe motorcycle-taxi protest/strike at a gendarmerie barrier near Bangui.

start_date.summary: Both reports place the January 7 barricade/protest on January 7.

end_date.summary: Both report that the barrier was removed or the route reopened after gendarmerie intervention/withdrawal; neither establishes when the strike or protest ended.

location.summary: Journal du Faso spells the road Nsila and places it about 11 km from Bangui; Oubangui Médias calls the gendarmerie barrier Nzila, also about 11 km south of Bangui. The spelling relationship should be checked.

scope.summary: One local road/barrier action is described; neither source identifies coordinated simultaneous actions elsewhere.

organizer.summary: A mototaxi syndicate is said to have requested that barriers be removed; neither report explicitly identifies the organizer of the Jan 7 action.

demands.summary: Drivers opposed gendarmerie-imposed formalities/fees and called for the barrier/gendarmes to leave. Coded under the original category for police brutality or arbitrary authority actions; no physical violence is reported.

participants_original.summary: Neither report gives a headcount. Oubangui Médias says nearby residents supported the demonstration, without a number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No numeric or clearly scaled crowd estimate establishes at least 50 people assembled simultaneously.

protester_violence.summary: Neither article describes violence by protesters; silence does not establish an explicit absence.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Gendarmes reportedly intervened/departed and the barrier was removed, but no agreement, negotiation or formal acceptance is described.

state_response.arrests.summary: Neither report mentions arrests of protesters.

state_response.beatings.summary: Neither report mentions beatings of protesters.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: A barrier was dismantled and gendarmes reportedly left; neither account says protesters were moved or the assembly dispersed.

state_response.ignore.summary: Gendarmerie intervention/departure is reported, so ignoring the action cannot be inferred; whether the grievance was addressed is unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: Neither report mentions deaths of protesters.

notes: Journal du Faso reports the Jan 7 strike and road barricade. Oubangui Médias separately describes a first Jan 5 sit-in and a Jan 7 demonstration at the gendarmerie barrier, including demands to end the fees and leave. The two outlets have different bylines and no shared origin is declared, but independence is not established. The 50-person threshold is not evidenced. Barrier removal/road reopening is not treated as proof that the protest ended; spelling variants Nsila/Nzila and the Jan 5-Jan 7 episode boundary remain open.
open_questions: How many demonstrators were assembled at one time?
Was there an identifiable organizer or group for the Jan 7 action?
Was the Jan 5 sit-in a discrete gathering or part of one continuing event culminating Jan 7?
Do Nsila and Nzila refer to the same barrier/location?
When did the Jan 7 strike/protest physically end, separately from removal of the barrier?
Did gendarmes move or disperse demonstrators, arrest, beat, or otherwise respond to them?
Can a third independent source confirm the gatherings and their scale?

title: Nzila/Nsila motorcycle-taxi sit-in against gendarmerie barrier
location: Nzila/Nsila gendarmerie barrier, about 11 km south of Bangui
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Oubangui Médias describes a sit-in on January 5 but gives no attendance estimate or clear scale of the assembled group.

title.summary: The report identifies an initial mototaxi sit-in at the Nzila gendarmerie barrier.

start_date.summary: The account explicitly dates the first sit-in to Thursday, January 5, 2023.

end_date.summary: The article later describes a Jan 7 action but does not state when the Jan 5 sit-in ended.

location.summary: The report’s context concerns the gendarmerie barrier at Nzila, about 11 km from Bangui; exact site attribution for the Jan 5 sit-in should be confirmed.

scope.summary: One local sit-in is described; no simultaneous broader action is reported.

organizer.summary: A mototaxi syndicate had petitioned authorities about barrier removal, but the report does not explicitly say it organized the Jan 5 sit-in.

demands.summary: The surrounding report identifies objection to gendarmerie-imposed formalities/fees and a demand that the barrier/gendarmes leave; this fits the original category for arbitrary authority actions. No physical brutality is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The word sit-in establishes a reported gathering but the account gives no number or clear qualitative scale supporting 50.

protester_violence.summary: No violence by protesters is described; absence is not coded.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The source does not attribute a negotiation, agreement or formal response to the Jan 5 sit-in.

state_response.arrests.summary: No arrest is reported for the Jan 5 sit-in.

state_response.beatings.summary: No beating is reported for the Jan 5 sit-in.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No dispersal action is described for the Jan 5 sit-in.

state_response.ignore.summary: The source does not establish whether authorities ignored the Jan 5 action.

state_response.killings.summary: No death is reported for the Jan 5 sit-in.

state_response.shootings.summary: No shooting is reported for the Jan 5 sit-in.

notes: Oubangui Médias places an initial sit-in on January 5, two days before a further January 7 demonstration/blockade at the same gendarmerie barrier. The account does not establish whether the gatherings were separate events or one continuing event. This remains a distinct provisional candidate linked by episode_key; no merge is implied. Attendance is unreported.
open_questions: Were at least 50 people assembled at the Jan 5 sit-in?
Was its precise location the Nzila/Nsila barrier?
Was the Jan 5 sit-in a separate event or part of the Jan 7 action?
Who organized the sit-in?
Did it physically end on Jan 5, and what response followed?

title: Nationwide primary and secondary teachers’ strike for status and pay
location: Nationwide; school stoppages reported in Bangui, Boali, Bossangoa, Berberati, Bria and Sibut
organizer: Dynamique des fédérations des enseignants du Fondamental 1,2 et de l’Enseignement Technique (SYNEAC, STD and FET; attribution from a later federation statement)
participants_original: No event-specific count. Education International later said the teachers’ strikes collectively mobilized massively nationwide; it did not isolate the January 31–February 2 action.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established for a public gathering. Radio Ndeke Luka reports schools closed or classes halted in several towns but gives no assembly count. Education International later described the strikes collectively as massively mobilized nationwide, without isolating this strike or a gathering. School closures, affected classes and teacher workforce size are not participant counts.

title.summary: Radio Ndeke Luka reports the teachers’ strike; Education International identifies a three-day national strike.

start_date.summary: The sources place the start on January 31, 2023.

end_date.summary: Education International says teachers observed the three-day strike from January 31 through February 2.

location.summary: The later federation account says the action was nationwide; Radio Ndeke Luka reports varied stoppages at named schools/towns.

scope.summary: The teachers’ platform called for a nationwide strike; report describes school stoppages across multiple parts of the country.

organizer.summary: Corbeau News attributes the Jan 31 strike notice to the teacher federations platform; Education International identifies its union members.

demands.summary: Corbeau News attributes salary, special-status, reinstatement and dialogue demands to the platform; Education International later gives fuller salary, allowance and work-condition demands for the wider strike series.

participants_original.summary: No event-specific count. Corbeau’s notice is conditional, and the later union-federation statement’s mass-participation phrase refers collectively to multiple strikes.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No event-specific assembly count is reported. The notice describes a planned work stoppage; the local report describes school closures; neither establishes a public gathering of at least 50.

public_assembly_evidence.summary: Corbeau describes a conditional strike notice, Radio Ndeke Luka reports work stoppages and a future assembly, and Education International reports a March assembly. No source documents an executed public assembly during the Jan 31-Feb 2 strike.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is reported; silence does not establish an explicit absence.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The minister said the department would respond in coming days; no completed negotiation or agreement concerning this specific strike is documented.

state_response.arrests.summary: Neither source reports arrests of teachers during this strike.

state_response.beatings.summary: Neither source reports beatings during this strike.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No protest gathering or dispersal mechanism during the strike is described.

state_response.ignore.summary: The ministry publicly said it would respond and the later federation alleges no positive movement across multiple strikes; response to this particular action remains unclear.

state_response.killings.summary: Neither source reports deaths of protesters during this strike.

state_response.shootings.summary: Neither source reports shooting during this strike.

notes: The three-day work stoppage began January 31 and ended February 2, so January owns this episode by start date. The sources document a nationwide labor action against state teacher policy but no public gathering during these dates; work stoppage alone, workforce size, school closures or affected students do not prove the codebook’s 50-person gathering criterion. The later Education International statement is a union-federation account that retrospectively covers several strikes; its qualitative “massively” wording is not assigned as an event-specific count. Pending evidence is retained for review, not as a proposed inclusion. Do not duplicate the same Jan31-Feb2 action as a February event. Corbeau News’ notice article identifies the platform’s particular wage/status/reinstatement demands but was published February 1 and does not itself confirm the strike occurred; occurrence is attributed to Radio Ndeke Luka’s Jan 31 coverage and Education International’s later retrospective.
open_questions: Did teachers hold any public meeting, march or other gathering during January 31-February 2?
Is there an event-specific turnout estimate or clear threshold description?
Which demands were formally tied to this particular three-day action?
What state response, if any, followed this strike?
Ensure a February unit treats this as a continuation by January ownership, not as a new event.

title: Anti-Castel demonstrations and product boycott in Bangui
location: Bangui, at multiple city sites including the MOCAF brewery and places displaying its branding
participants_original: Hamama Média's Q006 search-result snippet gives about twenty demonstrators at the brewery in mid-January; the article body was inaccessible, and this does not establish total participation across the reported Bangui locations.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The report refers to citizens at several locations and a group of activists visiting sites, but gives no count assembled at one time.

title.summary: ActuNiger describes protests and a boycott against Castel in Bangui.

start_date.summary: The article is dated January 23 and calls the activity recent; January is retained at month precision, while the exact first day remains unknown.

end_date.summary: The report gives no end date or final activity date.

location.summary: The report names Bangui and refers to several city locations, including sites with Castel branding and the brewery.

scope.summary: The report describes activity at multiple locations within Bangui, not a documented national organization.

organizer.summary: The report refers to citizens and a group of activists but names no organizer.

demands.summary: The reported demand is for the company to leave the country; the source does not state that protesters directed a demand to the government, so no original demand category is assigned.

participants_original.summary: The search-result snippet only reports about twenty at the brewery in mid-January; the article body was not accessible, so retain this as an unverified lead rather than a fully checked turnout estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: ActuNiger gives no count at any one gathering. A Hamama search-result snippet suggests about twenty at the brewery, but the article body was inaccessible and no count is given for activity at other sites; 50 or more at one time is not established.

protester_violence.summary: The report describes bottle-breaking against Castel products/property, but does not report violence against the state.

state_response.beatings.summary: No beatings by state agents are described.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No state dispersal response is described.

state_response.ignore.summary: The source does not report whether authorities ignored the action or responded.

notes: Retained for coordinator screening because ActuNiger reports public anti-company protest activity. A Hamama search-result snippet suggests about twenty at the brewery in mid-January, but its body was inaccessible and that number cannot be treated as total activity across locations. The ActuNiger source documents a demand for Castel to leave, not a demand on the home government; turnout at any single gathering is unverified. Neither government targeting nor the 50-person threshold is established, so this is not proposed as an eligible event. January is month-level only because the January 23 report calls the activity recent.
open_questions: Did any single public gathering reach at least 50 people?
Was the protest directed at the government or state policy, rather than only at the company?
What were the exact dates and locations of each action, and were they one organized episode or separate actions?
Who organized the actions?
What state response, if any, followed?
Can an independent source establish these fields and the relationship, if any, among multiple reports?
Can the Hamama snippet's approximate brewery turnout be confirmed from an accessible source, and were any other single gatherings larger?

title: Bangui bus and taxi drivers’ work stoppage over fuel and transport pricing
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Search-result excerpts describe drivers parking vehicles and stopping work but give no co-located gathering or attendance count. Vehicles, transport interruptions, drivers as a workforce and affected commuters are not participant counts.

title.summary: The UN report snippet and Oubangui Médias search excerpt both describe a January 5 bus-driver stoppage; Oubangui also mentions taxi drivers.

start_date.summary: Both search excerpts date the stoppage to January 5, 2023.

end_date.summary: The Oubangui search excerpt says one driver expected a three-day stoppage but also says some taxis resumed before noon; no final end date is confirmed.

location.summary: Both accounts place the drivers/action in Bangui.

scope.summary: The reports describe transport drivers in Bangui; no national organization is documented.

organizer.summary: An Oubangui excerpt says the union secretary general stated that its bureau had not authorized a strike; no organizing body for the stoppage is established.

demands.summary: The UN report snippet says drivers demanded an increase in transport fares from the government after the fuel-price rise; Oubangui describes protest against the fuel-price increase. This is coded provisionally as price/transport policy, pending body review.

participants_original.summary: Neither search excerpt gives a headcount.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The accounts document a work stoppage and parked vehicles but no gathering of 50 or more at one time; route disruption or workforce size is not turnout.

public_assembly_evidence.summary: The excerpts describe stopped work and parked vehicles only; no march, rally, sit-in or public gathering is specified.

protester_violence.summary: Search-result excerpts do not describe violence against the state.

state_response.accommodation.summary: A UN snippet records a government fare demand; Oubangui quotes a union official saying discussions with authorities were ongoing, but no meeting tied to this action or agreement is established.

state_response.arrests.summary: Search-result excerpts do not mention arrests; no body was read.

state_response.beatings.summary: Search-result excerpts do not mention beatings; no body was read.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No crowd or dispersal is described in the search-result excerpts.

state_response.ignore.summary: The excerpts mention policy communication and talks but do not establish whether authorities ignored this stoppage.

state_response.killings.summary: Search-result excerpts do not mention deaths; no body was read.

state_response.shootings.summary: Search-result excerpts do not mention shootings; no body was read.

notes: This January 5 bus/taxi stoppage is kept distinct from the same-day Nsila/Nzila mototaxi action at a gendarmerie barrier: the groups, locations and stated grievances differ. The report excerpts describe vehicles parked and work stopped over fuel/transport pricing but do not document a public gathering or turnout. The original manual requires a gathering of at least 50 making a demand of the home government; the current evidence supports a government transport-policy demand but does not establish the gathering threshold. Eligibility therefore remains pending, not approved.
open_questions: Did 50 or more drivers gather together in a public forum, or was this solely a work stoppage with scattered parked vehicles?
How many drivers were present at one time, and where?
Was the stoppage one continuous three-day action or did some drivers resume earlier?
Who organized the action, given that the union official reportedly disavowed authorization?
What response did the government make to the drivers’ request?
Can the UN report and local report be corroborated through accessible full text or independent accounts?
